question: M7
answer:
ANSWER

1. Current specification of HTTP/2: RFC 9113.
2. RFCs that RFC 9113 obsoletes: RFC 7540 and RFC 8740 (two documents, no others).

As-of date for the 'current' determination: 2026-11-16 (the date the cited primary sources were fetched). No later RFC obsoleting or replacing RFC 9113 appears in the sources consulted.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. THE CURRENT HTTP/2 SPECIFICATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------

RFC number:   9113
Title:        HTTP/2
Published:    June 2022
Stream:       IETF (HTTP working group)
Category:     Standards Track (RFC Editor metadata records the publication
              status as "PROPOSED STANDARD"; the document's Status of This
              Memo says "Internet Standards Track document")
Authors:      M. Thomson, Ed. (Mozilla); C. Benfield, Ed. (Apple Inc.)
DOI:          10.17487/RFC9113
Source draft: draft-ietf-httpbis-http2bis-07
Length:       78 pages
Errata:       https://www.rfc-editor.org/errata/rfc9113 (errata exist;
              errata do not change the specification's identity)

Evidence (primary sources, verbatim):

  a) RFC 9113 document header:
     "RFC: 9113 / Obsoletes: 7540, 8740 / Category: Standards Track /
      Published: June 2022"

  b) RFC 9113 abstract:
     "This specification describes an optimized expression of the semantics
      of the Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP), referred to as HTTP version
      2 (HTTP/2). ... This document obsoletes RFCs 7540 and 8740."

  c) RFC Editor metadata (rfc9113.json):
     "doc_id: RFC9113 / title: HTTP/2 / pub_status: PROPOSED STANDARD /
      status: PROPOSED STANDARD / source: HTTP / pub_date: June 2022 /
      obsoletes: RFC7540 / obsoletes: RFC8740"

  d) RFC Editor info page for RFC 9113 repeats the same header, abstract and
     obsoletes relation.

Corroborating (secondary) source: ITU-T J.484 reference entry states "IETF
RFC 9113 (2022) ... Title: HTTP/2 ... Obsoletes RFC 7540, RFC 8740." Used only
as corroboration; the RFC Editor metadata is authoritative.

Why 9113 and not 7540: RFC 7540 ("Hypertext Transfer Protocol Version 2
(HTTP/2)", May 2015, Belshe/Peon/Thomson) is the *original* HTTP/2
specification and is itself listed in RFC 9113's Obsoletes header. RFC 7540 is
therefore superseded and is not the current specification. RFC 9113 is the
revision that replaced it (the httpbis "http2bis" work item).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
2. WHAT RFC 9113 OBSOLETES
--------------------------------------------------------------------

The obsoletes relation is exactly two RFCs, taken from the document's own
header metadata (not from prose summaries, and not from its reference list):

  RFC 7540 — "Hypertext Transfer Protocol Version 2 (HTTP/2)",
             May 2015, Standards Track (Belshe, Peon, Thomson).
             The original HTTP/2 specification.

  RFC 8740 — "Using TLS 1.3 with HTTP/2", February 2020.
             Folded into RFC 9113; Appendix B states: "Use of TLS 1.3 was
             defined based on [RFC8740], which this document obsoletes."

That is the complete set. Verification notes:

  - The Obsoletes header lists only "7540, 8740"; the abstract says only
    "RFCs 7540 and 8740"; the machine-readable metadata has exactly two
    "obsoletes:" entries. All three agree, so there is no ambiguity to
    resolve.
  - RFC 9113 carries no "Updates" header and the metadata records no
    "updates:" relation. Obsolescence and update are distinct relations and
    must not be merged; nothing is added to the list on an "updates" basis.
  - Documents that RFC 9113 merely *references* are NOT obsoleted. In
    particular RFC 7541 (HPACK) is a normative reference and remains current;
    RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics) and RFC 9000 (QUIC) are references, not
    obsoletes. Do not extend the list with them.
  - RFC 7540's own history does not propagate: RFC 9113 obsoletes 7540 and
    8740 only. There is no transitive closure to compute.
  - RFC 9113 additionally *deprecates* certain mechanisms (the RFC 7540
    priority scheme; the HTTP/1.1 Upgrade / h2c path) and marks the
    HTTP2-Settings header field and h2c upgrade token as obsolete in its IANA
    Considerations. Those are deprecations of protocol features, not RFC-level
    obsolescence, and are excluded from the answer to ask 2.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
3. PROCEDURE USED (reproducible check)
--------------------------------------------------------------------

To re-verify at any future date, in this order:

  1. Fetch https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9113.json and read the
     "obsoletes:" fields. This is the authoritative machine-readable record.
  2. Confirm no successor exists: check the RFC Editor index / datatracker for
     any RFC whose "obsoletes:" metadata contains 9113, and check whether
     rfc9113.json has acquired an "obsoleted_by" relation. If a successor
     exists, ask 1's answer changes to that RFC and ask 2's answer becomes that
     successor's Obsoletes list.
  3. Cross-check the plain-text/HTML header block of the candidate document
     ("Obsoletes:" line) against the JSON. Prose abstracts are corroboration
     only; the header/metadata is controlling.
  4. Do not accept blog posts, vendor documentation, MDN, or Wikipedia as the
     source of the obsolescence relation.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4. SCOPE CAVEATS
--------------------------------------------------------------------

  - "Current" is time-indexed. This answer is stated as of 2026-11-16 and is
    falsified by any future RFC carrying "Obsoletes: 9113".
  - "Specification of HTTP/2" here means the primary HTTP/2 protocol
    specification, not extensions or companion documents (e.g., HTTP/2
    priority signaling, HPACK, or HTTP semantics), which are separate RFCs and
    are not the subject of either ask.
  - Obsolescence of a document is not a claim that its implementations are
    invalid; RFC 7540's protocol behavior is largely carried forward into
    RFC 9113, with the substantive changes enumerated in RFC 9113 Appendix B.
cautions: The recompute vote disagrees with this answer on ask 2.
confirmations: The figures this answer gives for ask 1, 2 stand in a passage found on its page.

asks.quote: Which RFC is the current specification of HTTP/2,

samples.title: HTTP/2
samples.status: Standards Track (RFC Editor JSON lists PROPOSED STANDARD; both indicate current IETF standard)
samples.note: RFC 9113 is the latest in the HTTP/2 specification lineage and is not itself obsoleted by any later RFC as of the fetch date.
